The tests depend on live multimodal provider requests or Python fixtures rather than synthetic Go values.
acceptance: TestCompressionContentLength_PlainString counts a 500-character string as 500 chars and preserves existing budget math expectations.
TestCompressionContentLength_MultimodalTextAndImage counts only text fields from mixed text/image blocks, not len(list).
TestCompressionContentLength_BareStringsInList covers []any{"hello", map[string]any{"text":"extra"}} without panic and sums both text sources.
TestCompressionContentLength_UnknownListItemFallback converts non-map/non-string list items with fmt.Sprint or equivalent deterministic fallback.
TestCompressionContentLength_ImageOnlyBlockZeroText proves image-only maps contribute zero text chars before the caller adds per-message overhead.
item.note: Complete: TDD added internal/llm/context_compressor_content.go and internal/llm/context_compressor_content_test.go. The pure compressionContentLength helper counts plain strings by rune length, sums text fields in mixed multimodal blocks, counts bare string list items, falls back to fmt.Sprint for unknown non-map/non-string list items, and treats image-only blocks as zero text chars before any caller overhead. item.name: Gormes-owned session tree navigator over lineage and labels

TestTitleFailureCallback_SwallowsCallbackError proves sink errors return callback_failed evidence without panicking or changing the foreground turn result.

item.name: Busy command guard for compression and long CLI actions
item.contract: Long-running CLI commands set busy input state and reject overlapping user input until the command exits
item.degraded_mode: CLI/TUI status reports command-busy state instead of accepting overlapping input that can corrupt turn state.
ready_when: The CLI command registry has a shared active-turn/busy policy surface.
not_ready_when: Busy state is implemented only for /compress or only in the visual TUI without a command-layer invariant.
blocked_by: CLI command registry parity + active-turn busy policy
acceptance: /compress and other long-running command handlers set and clear busy state even on error.
User input during busy command execution returns a visible busy response.
The guard does not block gateway-safe commands that explicitly declare active-turn bypass.
item.note: Complete: TDD landed `BusyCommandGuard` in `internal/cli/busy_command.go` with `Run(name, status, fn)` that sets command-busy state, defers a clearing closure so success, error, and panic exit paths all reset the flag, and rejects nested entries with `ErrBusyCommandActive` (empty names rejected with `ErrBusyCommandInvalid`). The guard exposes `IsBusy`, `Status`, `ActiveCommand`, and `EvaluateInput` for the input dispatcher; `EvaluateInput` consults `ResolveCommandPolicy` so any command declared `ActiveTurnPolicyBypass` (`/help`, `/stop`, `/restart`) passes through while the guard is busy, and every other input — plain text, recognized non-bypass slash, or unknown slash — gets a uniform `Gormes is busy — <status> — wait for it to finish or send /stop` notice that includes the active status label. `internal/tui/model.go` adds an `Options.BusyGuard BusyInputEvaluator` interface so the kernel package stays independent of `internal/cli`; `internal/tui/update.go` consults the guard in the `tea.KeyEnter` branch before slash dispatch and submit, so a rejected verdict resets the editor, surfaces the evidence as `statusMessage`, and skips both the slash registry and the Submitter callback. Tests cover idle baseline, busy-during-fn, success/error/panic clear, nested rejection, idle-accepts-anything, plain-text rejection, bypass allow-list (incl. mixed-case `/STOP`), non-bypass slash rejection, unknown slash rejection, evidence-mentions-status, concurrent EvaluateInput across goroutines, ActiveCommand reporting, and empty-name rejection. The TUI fixture asserts plain text is consumed without calling Submitter while busy, that idle evaluators preserve the existing submit path, and that bypass slash commands still dispatch through the slash registry while busy.
done_signal: Busy-command fixtures prove overlapping input is rejected while long-running CLI commands execute and busy state clears on every exit path.

item.name: Hermes sessions CLI MRU browse/delete ergonomics
item.contract: `gormes sessions` matches Hermes operator ergonomics over the native session store: `-c`/continue resolves the most recently active session by last_active before started_at and is not limited to the newest started 20 rows; delete accepts unique ID prefixes and reports not found without mutating; delete/prune confirmation handles EOF/non-TTY as cancelled; browse offers an interactive picker with title-over-preview display and a numbered fallback when curses/TUI selection is unavailable; and unquoted multi-word session names are coalesced before subcommands.

The browse fallback requires curses, Bubble Tea, a browser, or a live terminal to pass.
Delete/prune proceeds after EOF, missing confirmation, ambiguous prefix, or not-found resolution.

item.name: Cross-session memory continuity
item.contract: Memories persist across sessions with continuity guarantees. When a new session starts, the agent retrieves relevant past memories automatically (not all memories — relevance-filtered). Agent detects contradictions between old and new information and resolves them.
source_refs: Generative Agents memory stream (Park et al. 2023)
ready_when: Memory tools exist (6.J row 1)
Goncho supports session-scoped queries
not_ready_when: Memory is session-scoped only (no cross-session persistence)
acceptance: New session auto-loads top-K relevant memories from prior sessions
Agent can query 'what do I know about X' across all sessions
Contradiction detection: new fact conflicts with stored fact → agent prompted to resolve
Memory writes are session-attributed with provenance
Session deletion can optionally preserve or cascade-delete memories
item.note: Complete: TDD expanded cross-session continuity beyond the placeholder loader. `MemoryToolEntry` now carries `session_id`, `LocalMarkdownMemoryStore.Store` persists explicit or configured session provenance, and retrieval returns session metadata so a new session can load relevant prior-session memories without loading unrelated memories. `CrossSessionMemory.QueryKnowledge` answers cross-session knowledge queries with memory results, per-session counts, and a source-id summary. `contradiction_detector.go` adds deterministic same-subject/same-relation conflict detection while allowing additive facts such as `uses Python` -> `uses Python and Go`. `PlanSessionMemoryDeletion` records preserve-vs-cascade behavior so session deletion can retain memories by default or cascade-forget session-attributed memories explicitly.
done_signal: Cross-session tests prove memories survive session boundaries and new sessions auto-load relevant context
